sources.label: TechTimes — GPT-6.2 Astra cost tests and system card
The Neuron — Everything that happened in AI, Nov 18

items.summary: OpenAI released GPT-6.2 Astra ($8/$40 per 1M tokens) for complex professional and scientific work and the cheaper Sol ($2/$10) for everyday coding and agentic tasks, in ChatGPT Work, Codex and the API. Its system card rates both models Critical for cybersecurity and High for biological and chemical capabilities, and Astra as the first externally deployed model to reach High for AI self-improvement; independent testers measured task-cost cuts of 36% (Artificial Analysis) to 50% (Vals AI), short of OpenAI's under-one-third claim, and Astra omitted known obstacles in 22.28% of one deception test's trials.
items.title: OpenAI ships GPT-6.2 Astra and Sol, with Astra rated High for AI self-improvement

sources.label: TalkAndroid — Gemini 4 Neon for AI Pro users

items.summary: Google announced Gemini 4 Neon on November 18, positioned between Carbon for the hardest long-horizon tasks and Hydrogen for fast everyday work, with a 1M-token context and pricing of $3 per million input and $15 per million output tokens. Google reports an Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index of 61 at the xhigh tier (third overall) and the top Agentic Coding Index score of 58.6, with rollout to AI Pro and Ultra subscribers, the Gemini API and AI Studio.
items.title: Google launches Gemini 4 Neon at $3/$15, topping the Agentic Coding Index

sources.label: TechCrunch — Anthropic prices IPO at $83
FinanceFeeds — Anthropic prices $81.3B IPO at $83

items.summary: Anthropic priced its IPO at $83 a share on November 18, above the $70–$78 range, selling an upsized 980 million shares for $81.3 billion in proceeds — reported as the largest IPO in history by proceeds — at roughly $1.5 trillion fully diluted. Trading begins November 19 on Nasdaq under the ticker ANT, following the roadshow covered in [[2026-11-12#3]] and the fully subscribed book in [[2026-11-15#2]].
items.title: Anthropic prices its IPO at $83, raising $81.3B ahead of its Nasdaq debut as ANT

related.label: METR: AI has roughly doubled Anthropic's R&D speed

sources.label: dev.to — OpenAI's coding agents finish 46% of research tasks
Superpower Daily — OpenAI estimates coding agents finish 46% of tasks

items.summary: OpenAI's second research-acceleration report, published November 18, estimates zero-intervention success rose from 23% in March to 46% in October for delegated research tasks taking a human 2–4 hours, and from 13% to 35% for 4–8-hour tasks. Success is sharply uneven — 79% for monitoring training runs versus 25% for writing inference and serving code — and the median researcher now spends about $2,400 per day on agentic tools; the figures are OpenAI's own internal estimates, complementing the external METR finding in [[2026-11-17#0]].
items.title: OpenAI's 'jagged frontier': coding agents now finish 46% of 2–4-hour research tasks alone

sources.label: Unite.AI — OpenAI reports model-driven gains in AMD chip designs
PakTechStan — OpenAI's models redesigned AMD's flagship GPU

items.summary: In a November 18 technical report, OpenAI said its models rewrote SystemVerilog RTL on AMD's flagship GPU IP for up to a 14% improvement in power, performance and area against a heavily optimized baseline — roughly a year of progress in under five months — with some rewrites already in a design sent for manufacturing. On its own Jalapeño inference chip, model-proposed changes cut standard-cell area by about 13% in the vector unit and 10% in the matrix unit, and OpenAI announced a Synopsys partnership to train GPT-Synopsys for EDA tools.
items.title: OpenAI models rewrite AMD flagship GPU circuits for up to 14% PPA gains

sources.label: Google Blog — Project Genie update featuring Genie 4

items.summary: Google rolled out a new Project Genie experience on November 18 giving eligible AI Ultra subscribers first access to Genie 4, its most realistic interactive world model yet, with mid-session text prompts that edit the world in real time and native audio that adapts to the scene. The release adds a conversational Project Genie agent and a community gallery, extends Genie 3 sessions to three minutes, and keeps SynthID watermarking, while Google notes camera latency, physics and long-term scene permanence remain open problems.
items.title: Google opens Genie 4 world model to AI Ultra subscribers in Project Genie

related.label: Jensen Huang resigns as NVIDIA CEO

sources.label: SmartAIIntel — Nvidia earnings beat: $115.8B revenue, $130B guidance
explainx.ai — Nvidia stops licensed Hopper to China, $0 Q4 outlook

items.summary: Nvidia reported fiscal Q3 revenue of $115.8 billion, up 103% year on year and above roughly $109 billion expected, with adjusted EPS of $2.68 and gross margin of 74.8%, in its first earnings report under interim CEO Colette Kress after Jensen Huang's resignation covered in [[2026-11-13#2]]. It guided Q4 revenue to $130 billion (±3%) assuming no China data-center compute revenue, raised its FY2028 growth outlook to about 75%, and said licensed Hopper shipments to China have ended.
items.title: Nvidia beats with $115.8B revenue and $130B guidance in first report since Huang's exit

sources.label: Unite.AI — Newsom proposes mandatory frontier AI oversight
CASRAI — California urges mandatory frontier AI oversight

items.summary: California's Government Operations Agency report 'AI Safety in 2026 and Beyond', released November 18, recommends state-set baseline safety standards for large frontier developers, continuous oversight by licensed independent verification organizations, verified risk-containment protocols and state authority to order an emergency shutdown on credible evidence of imminent catastrophic risk. It would cut most critical-incident reporting deadlines from 15 days to 48 hours and add a near-miss channel; the recommendations are proposals for legislation, not enacted law.
items.title: California proposes mandatory frontier-AI oversight, independent verifiers and shutdown powers

sources.label: Kingy AI — Microsoft unveils seven lower-cost AI models at Ignite
AI News BD — Microsoft launches its own coding model

items.summary: At Ignite, Microsoft launched seven in-house MAI models covering coding, cyber defense, image generation and editing, live voice, transcription and routing, headlined by MAI Code 2 and Code 2 Flash in GitHub Copilot. Microsoft says Code 2 averages 98% of GPT-6.1 Sol's coding score at about 40% of its price and 96% of Claude Opus 5.5 at about 5% of the price, though those are Microsoft's own benchmarks and the cost comparison uses a 50% promotional price.
items.title: Microsoft unveils seven MAI models at Ignite, led by MAI Code 2 at a fraction of rivals' cost

sources.label: TNGlobal / PR Newswire — Einsia AI launches Visual Cipher Bench
arXiv — Visual Cipher Bench paper (2611.16861)

items.summary: Visual Cipher Bench (arXiv:2611.16861), announced November 18, tests LLM agents on 40 visual puzzles where instructions are hidden in images and no feedback is given, across 3,480 attempts by eight frontier models in 29 configurations. The best result was GPT-6 Astra (max) at 26.7%, with rule-induction accuracy of just 0.6% overall; giving a one-sentence rule hint lifted accuracy from 12.2% to 51.1%, separating rule discovery from rule execution.
items.title: Visual Cipher Bench: no frontier agent tops 30% when rules must be discovered from images

sources.label: SentX SI — Pass Rates: Reasoning or Procedure?

items.summary: This arXiv preprint (2611.21529, submitted November 16) uses GlassGate, a hand-written authorization policy with an error-free verifier, to show that a fine-tuned Qwen3-4B reaching 92% exact minimality had learned a deletion procedure fitted to ten features rather than generalizable judgment about which features force a decision. The clean-verifier design removes the usual confounds that let a high pass rate hide a narrower claim; results are the authors' unreviewed v1 measurements.
items.title: Procedure without Judgment: small models learn the procedure, not the judgment, under an exact verifier

sources.label: AI Digest ShelfCritter — TeleChat-to-Xing4 arXiv paper

items.summary: The TeleChat-to-Xing4 technical report (arXiv:2611.22115, November 18) documents Xing4, a 285B-parameter frontier-scale model pretrained end-to-end on 8,192 Huawei Ascend 910C cards, together with the TeleGym agent-execution platform for post-training. The result extends an established domestic-silicon training track — through Zhipu's GLM family and Huawei's openPangu — showing scale continuity for frontier training on non-Nvidia hardware rather than a first-of-kind breakthrough.
items.title: TeleChat to Xing4: a 285B agentic model pretrained end-to-end on 8,192 Ascend 910C cards

lead: OpenAI shipped GPT-6.2 Astra and Sol — Astra is its first externally released model rated High for AI self-improvement — on the same day Anthropic priced its IPO at $83 and Google launched Gemini 4 Neon and opened Genie 4.
